name: PrimeTTS v2.1 Nano latency: 4 concurrent real-time requests, quality preserved

description: Baseline: 4 concurrent T81 requests on the Nano (resident GPU weights + per-stream arenas/streams), SNDR 70.08 dB

asi.hypothesis: establish the session baseline before any change
asi.noise_floor_note: N=4 wall measured 9917 ms and 10308 ms on two identical runs: ~4% run-to-run spread on the Nano; treat sub-4% deltas as noise
asi.phase_split: single stream T81: GPU kernels+sync 1673 ms, staging copies 39 ms, alloc/free 0; total run 4.44 s, so ~2.7 s is host graph work serialized against the GPU
asi.next_action_hint: attack the host side first (elementwise ops are scalar C; 4066 nodes; ~2.7 s of a 4.44 s stream)
asi.memory: free RAM dips to ~1119 MB with 4 streams at 32 MB arenas; guard is 60 MB so there is headroom

description: bin_op elementwise fast path (contiguous / scalar-broadcast fp32 ADD,SUB,MUL,DIV,MAX,MIN as plain vectorizable loops): ADD 349->108 ms, single stream 3863->3690 ms; N=4 wall unchanged within noise

asi.confidence: primary delta -0.7% is inside the ~4% Nano noise floor; kept because the op-level gain is measured (ADD 3.2x) and the change is a strict simplification with bit-exact output
asi.hypothesis: the interpreter's strided broadcast loop cannot be vectorized; give the contiguous and scalar-broadcast fp32 cases plain loops so gcc -O3 emits NEON on the A57
asi.next_action_hint: at N=4 the GPU is the shared bottleneck (conv kernels ~1.7 s serialized across streams). Attack conv kernel efficiency (cin split, threads, __ldg) and CUDA Graphs to remove ~180 launch+sync round trips per request. Remaining host items worth vectorizing: EINSUM 381 ms (2 calls), SLICE 207 ms, LEAKYRELU 200 ms
asi.result_detail: ADD 349.4->108.7 ms, MUL 99->63 ms; SNDR 70.08 dB and max|d| 2.247e-04 identical to baseline, so bit-exact as predicted
asi.why_n4_flat: at N=4 four streams contend for one GPU, so host-side savings show up in n1_stream_ms (-4.5%) and barely in n4_wall_ms

description: Share the host-side fp16->fp32 container conversions across contexts (ctab-keyed, refcounted, mutex-guarded): N=4 wall 10308->10072 ms (-2.3%, two runs), N=1 3690->3613 ms, free RAM +30 MB

asi.confidence: two runs 10070 and 10075 ms (0.05% spread) against baseline 10308: -2.3%, reproducible but modest; n1 3613/3668 vs 3690
asi.hypothesis: the 39 fp16 decoder records are 13.6M elements; each context converted them to its own 54.5 MB fp32 array, so four streams paid ~164 MB of duplicated host memory. Share the conversion across contexts (ctab-keyed, refcounted, mutex-guarded, container-path guarded)
asi.memory: min free RAM during N=4 on picard rose 1127 -> 1157 MB; the real relief is ~3x54 MB of host allocations removed, which matters most on pesi where N=4 measured only 66 MB free
asi.next_action_hint: host work is now ~1.1 s of a 3.6 s stream: EINSUM 377 ms in 2 calls is the single biggest non-GPU item, then SLICE 208 ms and LEAKYRELU 215 ms. At N=4 the wall is GPU-contention-bound (conv kernels ~1.7 s x 4 streams serialized), so the next big lever is GPU-side: CUDA Graphs per stream and conv kernel efficiency
asi.quality: SNDR 70.08 dB and max|d| 2.247e-04 bit-identical to baseline on both paths; sharing is safe because the conversion is a pure function of the container bytes

description: Per-context capacity-sorted buffer pool for activation tensors: no latency gain (10087 vs 10070 ms), costs ~200 MB retained RAM at N=4

asi.confidence: 10087 vs 10070 ms at N=4 (+0.2%, inside noise) and n1 3604 vs 3613: no speed signal, while min free RAM fell 1154 -> 955 MB
asi.hypothesis: thousands of malloc/free pairs per request dominate host time; a capacity-sorted per-context buffer pool should remove allocator traffic
asi.next_action_hint: host side: EINSUM 377 ms in 2 calls (iSTFT basis), SLICE 212 ms, LEAKYRELU 135 ms are the remaining big items, and tv_alloc's full-buffer memset is unmeasured cost worth probing. GPU side: conv kernels 1.7 s per stream at ~80% of the measured 62 GF/s fp32 peak, so kernel tiling is a 1.2-1.3x lever at best; the 180 per-op stream syncs are ~7 ms, so CUDA Graphs is a launch-hygiene win, not the bottleneck
asi.rollback_reason: no measurable latency gain (N=4 +0.2%, N=1 -0.2%, both inside the ~4% Nano noise floor) while costing ~200 MB of retained memory at N=4 (min free 1154 -> 955 MB) from the 48 MB per-stream pool cap. glibc's allocator was already reusing the freed blocks, so allocation cost was not the bottleneck
asi.quality: SNDR 70.08 dB, max|d| 2.247e-04, bit-identical to baseline: the pool itself was numerically clean

description: Specialized batched-matmul path for the iSTFT einsums (bkt,kn->bnt): EINSUM 377 ms -> below the 18 ms reporting floor; N=4 wall 10070 -> 9867 ms, N=1 3613 -> 3294 ms

asi.confidence: -2.0% on the primary against the previous best (10070 -> 9867) and -8.8% on n1 (3613 -> 3294 ms), well outside the noise on the single-stream number
asi.hypothesis: the two iSTFT einsums (`bkt,kn->bnt`, A=(4,9,3617) B=(9,16) O=(4,16,3617)) ran through the generic letter-space loop, which modulo-decodes every index per element: 377 ms for 231k FMAs. A specialized batched-matmul loop (innermost index contiguous in both A and the output, per-(b,n) double accumulator) removes the decode entirely.
asi.next_action_hint: host list is now LEAKYRELU 215 ms (35 calls, ~0.4 GB/s effective - suspiciously bandwidth-like, look at what else those nodes pay), SLICE 215 ms (214 calls), ADD 107, TANH 81 (libm per element), PAD 66. GPU: conv kernels 1682 ms of a 3.3 s stream.
asi.quality: SNDR 70.08 dB, max|d| 2.247e-04 - bit-identical to baseline: same summation order (summed index ascending) and same double accumulator, only the index arithmetic changed
asi.pitfall_found: first attempt accumulated every n into one shared scratch row (outputs got the sum over all n): SNDR -39 dB, shapes all correct. The scratch must be N*T, one k-sum per (b,n) output row
